summary.intent: Deploy v0.25.0 to staging, debug and fix a broken Docker API build, investigate staging performance issues (slow IPNS publish, broken token refresh), and refactor the web app's duplicated API client infrastructure.
summary.outcome: Successfully fixed the Docker API build (PR #308), consolidated the web app from 3 HTTP client paths to 1 by removing the orval-generated React Query client in favor of @cipherbox/api-client (PR #309), fixed IPNS publish latency by making DHT propagation fire-and-forget, and unblocked release-please after it got stuck on unparseable old PR titles.

repo: The API is a zero-knowledge server — it never handles plaintext or performs crypto, so it genuinely has no workspace package dependencies. The api-client package is the typed bridge generated from OpenAPI spec.

The web app had 3 separate HTTP client paths: orval-generated fetch (React Query hooks), a legacy axios client (login/vault init), and bare IPFS functions. Only ~1 endpoint actually used the React Query hooks; everything else called raw generated functions.

release-please scans ALL merged PRs in the repo regardless of bootstrap-sha. Renaming old PRs that match the release title pattern (but can't be parsed for component) is the only way to unblock it after a monorepo config migration.
The Tag Staging Release workflow is intentionally manual — it runs E2E tests and requires staging-approval before creating the staging RC tag and triggering deployment.
The staging deployment workflow triggers on tags matching v*-staging*, not on release tags — staging deploys are always initiated manually via the Tag Staging Release action.
Grafana Cloud free-tier instances hibernate and return 503 on first request after inactivity — transient and can be ignored if the dashboard was already provisioned.

The pull-request-title-pattern in release-please-config.json must include ${component} for multi-package monorepos, otherwise release-please can't match merged release PRs back to their packages and aborts with 'untagged merged release PRs outstanding'.

code.finding: DHT publish via someguy was awaited, causing 10-30s latency. DB record is saved synchronously first; delegated routing publish is now fire-and-forget with a trailing .catch() for logging. The result variable stays 'success' since DHT propagation is best-effort.

Added 401 response interceptor with shared-promise deduplication (single in-flight refresh), withCredentials for HTTP-only refresh token cookies, and onRefreshFailure callback. Uses AxiosHeaders.set() for safe header mutation.

Reduced from 131 to 70 lines by removing raw fetch path (which bypassed 401 interceptor). Both upload (with onUploadProgress) and download (with onDownloadProgress) now use the api-client axios instance consistently.
Single initialization point for setApiClientConfig — wires getAccessToken from Zustand store, withCredentials: true, and onRefreshFailure that calls clearAllUserStores and redirects to login.

The generated API client drift check was comparing all of packages/api-client/ — including instance.ts, tests, package.json — which would false-positive on any manual edits. Fixed to only diff openapi.json, src/generated/, and src/models/.

bootstrap-sha only affects commit scanning, not merged PR scanning. It does not prevent release-please from finding and failing on old unparseable release PRs. Removing custom pull-request-title-pattern lets release-please use its default monorepo format.

workflow: When release-please gets stuck on 'untagged merged release PRs', renaming the old PR titles via GitHub API (so they no longer match the release title pattern) is the fix — bootstrap-sha alone is insufficient.
For fire-and-forget promises in NestJS services, always add a trailing .catch() to prevent unhandled rejection warnings, and test it with a spy on the private Logger instance.
chore commits don't trigger release-please version bumps — use fix(ci) for broken build fixes to get a patch release.
After manually creating a tag/release to unblock staging, release-please may still need the branch deleted and PR titles cleaned up before it can create new release PRs.

When migrating from single-package to multi-package release-please config, all previously merged release PRs will have titles that the new pattern can't parse — rename them in bulk before the new config takes effect.

friction: release-please blocked on old merged PR titles across multiple fix attempts — bootstrap-sha, branch deletion, and config changes all failed before the root cause (PR title scanning ignores bootstrap-sha) was identified.
Needed multiple PRs (#307, #311, #312, #313) just to fix the release-please config, each requiring a merge to main to trigger a test run.
The Dockerfile had a stale packages/crypto COPY that introduced a transient build failure when the crypto package gained a new workspace dependency (@cipherbox/core).
The CI verify step was incorrectly scoped to all of packages/api-client/ instead of just the generated output directories, causing false failures.
Token refresh was silently broken for an unknown period — only exposed by a long-running batch operation that lasted longer than the 15-minute access token TTL.
open_items: React Query cache is not cleared on logout or token refresh failure — clearAllUserStores() clears Zustand but stale query data persists. Noted as a pre-existing gap, deferred as follow-up.

The slow IPNS publish fix (fire-and-forget DHT) is deployed but staging verification of the actual latency improvement hasn't been confirmed — the Tag Staging Release workflow was triggered but the session ended before results.
Token refresh fix (PR #309) was merged but not yet verified on staging via smoke tests — the original 401 issue that exposed the bug hasn't been re-tested.

SDK consumers of @cipherbox/api-client now get withCredentials: true globally, which may be undesirable for non-browser environments (desktop app, SDK). The onRefreshFailure callback needs to be wired appropriately for each consumer.

The IPNS SDK batch handling was noted as a potential separate issue contributing to slow batch deletes — the fire-and-forget fix addresses per-publish latency but true batching behavior in the SDK package was not investigated.
